question: The greatest integer that will divide \(13{,}511,\) \(13{,}903,\) and \(14{,}589\) and leave the same remainder is:
solution:
Equal remainders disappear when we subtract the numbers. Thus, if the positive integer \(d\) leaves the same remainder in all three divisions, it must divide
\[
13{,}903-13{,}511=392
\]
and
\[
14{,}589-13{,}903=686.
\]
It must therefore also divide
\[
2(392)-686=98.
\]
Consequently, \(d\leq 98\).

To show that this bound is attained, write
\[
\begin{aligned}
13{,}511&=98(137)+85,\\
13{,}903&=98(141)+85,\\
14{,}589&=98(148)+85.
\end{aligned}
\]
Since \(0\leq85<98\), these are valid divisions with the same remainder. The greatest divisor is therefore \(\boxed{98}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
